topic: Construct finite-sample replacement-DP honest confidence intervals for the pointwise Hölder CATE at an interior anchor under overlap, bounded common-support outcomes, and positive local design density. On the concrete uniform-design attainable subclass, build a fully private higher-order local learner with privatized nuisance pilots and localized linear and quadratic moments; prove an unrestricted-finite-rank remainder bound, a transcript-wise nonempty clipped interval, and an optimized expected-length upper phase separating privacy-free, ordinary private-regression, and higher-order global-sensitivity terms. On the unchanged full class, prove the ordinary γ-smooth honest-length lower bound and the fixed-dimensional β-smooth private direct-regression upper bound, and state the resulting nonsharp full-class and attainable-class brackets, including a public selector between the two attainable upper constructions. Keep the exact full-class nuisance/private-Gram confidence frontier open; no matched full-class phase is claimed.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the exact central approximate-DP minimax absolute-risk phase diagram for pointwise CATE on the unchanged Kennedy–Balakrishnan–Robins–Wasserman Hölder class, including whether the low-nuisance-smoothness privacy term is governed by q=alpha+beta or collapses to a gamma-smooth private-regression/private-Gram barrier.

source_refs.claim: Derives the privacy-free pointwise CATE minimax rate by localized fuzzy hypotheses and attains it, under stated density and Gram conditions, with a higher-order local-polynomial R-learner.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: Provides a central (epsilon,delta)-DP Neyman-orthogonal CATE framework and quasi-oracle conditions, but does not characterize minimax pointwise rates over the Hölder nuisance/CATE class.
source_refs.author: Maresa Schröder, Valentyn Melnychuk, Stefan Feuerriegel

source_refs.claim: Introduces a differentially private CATE meta-algorithm instantiated with private explainable boosting machines and reports empirical privacy-utility behavior rather than a Hölder minimax frontier.
source_refs.author: Fengshi Niu, Harsha Nori, Brian Quistorff, Rich Caruana, Donald Ngwe, Aadharsh Kannan
source_refs.venue: Conference on Causal Learning and Reasoning

open_problems.why_unsolved: The nonprivate paper separates an oracle gamma-regression regime from a low-smoothness regression/functional regime using localized fuzzy hypotheses, while the central-DP CATE papers establish privacy for meta-learners without a matching minimax lower bound on that class. No located theorem decides how replacement privacy interacts with the localized prior-mixture cancellation. The proposed q=alpha+beta exponent is therefore presolve evidence rather than a published fact: positivity, unchanged common support, n-sample mixture closeness, and low-cost approximate-DP transport must hold simultaneously, whereas an ordinary two-point perturbation exposes only the gamma-local-regression barrier.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A two-sided theorem giving minimax absolute risk as an explicit maximum of the privacy-free KBRW rate and piecewise privacy terms, with a proved phase boundary selecting the q=alpha+beta branch or a gamma/private-Gram branch for every admissible (alpha,beta,gamma,d,epsilon_n,delta_n).

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves from heterogeneous effects to an unresolved optimality question and organizes the answer as a matched lower/upper minimax phase theorem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: CATE is a regression target contaminated by unknown causal nuisances -> low nuisance smoothness creates a regression/functional hybrid -> privacy adds a second information bottleneck whose exact phase branch must be identified

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the localized fuzzy-hypothesis lower bound and higher-order local-polynomial R-learner, including the localized projection, bias decomposition, and quadratic U-statistic variance proof, while adding privacy terms.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It proves the exact privacy-free theorem on the destination Hölder CATE model, so the private theorem must reduce to its rate and constructions as epsilon tends to infinity.

method_exemplars.technique: Use private Le Cam and Assouad inequalities proved through couplings whose expected sample Hamming distance controls the privacy penalty.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The missing lower-bound step is precisely a coupling-to-private-testing reduction for neighboring fuzzy-mixture coordinates.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the bias-variance-sensitivity optimization and pointwise private-regression lower-bound calculation, accounting for its distributed-DP rather than single-curator experiment.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives the nearest proved pointwise smooth-regression privacy phase, supplying the gamma-only benchmark that the causal nuisance branch must beat or match.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop a paired-cell approximate-DP tracing theorem for localized causal functionals that converts prior-averaged observational cancellation and a low expected record-Hamming coupling into a sharp pointwise minimax lower bound while retaining strictly positive common-support laws.

source_refs.claim: Its CATE lower bound uses specially localized fuzzy hypotheses and controls Hellinger distance between mixtures of n-fold product laws.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: Relates couplings and expected Hamming distance to central-DP analogues of Assouad, Fano, and Le Cam lower bounds.
source_refs.author: Jayadev Acharya, Ziteng Sun, Huanyu Zhang

source_refs.claim: Develops a tracing-based score attack for private minimax lower bounds and applies it to Sobolev nonparametric regression, but assumes a usable score model rather than a causal fuzzy-mixture cancellation.
source_refs.author: T. Tony Cai, Yichen Wang, Linjun Zhang

source_refs.claim: Extends fingerprinting lower bounds to approximate-DP estimation and obtains a sharp mean-estimation bound using private Assouad.
source_refs.author: Gautam Kamath, Argyris Mouzakis, Vikrant Singhal

source_refs.excerpt: The likelihood comparison is taken with respect to O_T only and includes every initial window t≤Q.
The proof must verify the conditional likelihood factorization uniformly for every Q,T.

open_problems.why_unsolved: KBRW controls divergence of prior mixtures after nuisance perturbations cancel in the observational experiment; private Assouad instead requires coordinatewise couplings with low expected sample Hamming distance, and score or fingerprinting attacks use regular score/exponential-family structure absent from the fuzzy causal mixture. The prior POMDP proposal independently exposes the analogous gap between hiding a target-relevant sign on the observed filtration and proving the full n-sample likelihood comparison. For DP-CATE the first changed step is exact eta/tau paired-cell cancellation followed by an n-sample coupling whose Hamming cost stays on the alpha+beta scale under replacement adjacency and approximate-DP delta leakage. The finite square-partition kill test must rule out the possibility that positivity forces every feasible coupling back to gamma scale.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A general lemma bounding every replacement-(epsilon,delta)-DP estimator's risk from paired prior mixtures via target separation, residual mixture divergence, and expected n-sample Hamming cost, plus a positive common-support CATE corollary with the q exponent or a finite-microcell dual certificate proving an unavoidable gamma-scale cost.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames a reusable private information-theoretic lemma first and then demonstrates its value through sharp model-specific corollaries.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Classical testing reductions miss privacy cost -> coupling exposes record changes visible to DP -> a causal paired-mixture version decides the disputed CATE privacy branch

method_exemplars.technique: Couple neighboring hypercube-coordinate product distributions and insert expected Hamming distance into the private Assouad testing inequality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired theorem has the same output—a private minimax risk lower bound—but begins with paired prior mixtures rather than ordinary coordinate laws.

method_exemplars.technique: Use localized fuzzy priors whose averaged densities cancel nuisance perturbations while preserving separation in tau(x0), together with n-fold mixture Hellinger control.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the source construction to preserve; the new proof replaces its terminal nonprivate testing step with privacy-sensitive Hamming transport.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt generalized fingerprinting and private-Assouad arguments that keep approximate-DP delta terms explicit.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a model for controlling approximate-DP leakage when elementary pure-DP group-privacy arguments are too costly.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a fully replacement-(epsilon_n,delta_n)-DP stabilized higher-order local-polynomial R-learner for pointwise CATE in which nuisance pilots, localized basis moments, Gram matrices and inverses, and quadratic correction terms are all privatized under one auditable budget and attain the lower-bound phase rate on the same Hölder class.

source_refs.claim: The nonprivate attaining estimator depends on independent nuisance and density pilots, bounded localized Gram inverses, and a quadratic higher-order correction.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: Privatizes two-stage Neyman-orthogonal CATE learners through private nuisance estimates and target perturbation, with quasi-oracle conditions rather than KBRW-class rate optimality.
source_refs.author: Maresa Schröder, Valentyn Melnychuk, Stefan Feuerriegel

source_refs.claim: Gives central-DP positive-definite approximations of finite-dimensional second-moment matrices with utility guarantees for linear regression.
source_refs.author: Or Sheffet

source_refs.claim: Calibrates Gaussian-process noise to RKHS sensitivity for private release of function-valued estimators.
source_refs.author: Rob Hall, Alessandro Rinaldo, Larry Wasserman

open_problems.why_unsolved: The KBRW proof treats fitted propensity, outcome, covariate distribution, localized projection matrix, and inverse Gram as nonprivate inputs satisfying high-level bounds; its quadratic correction also has bandwidth- and basis-dimension-dependent sensitivity. DP-CATE handles ordinary orthogonal learners but does not analyze the localized higher-order U-statistic or the KBRW low-smoothness rate. Private second-moment methods ensure positive definiteness in fixed-dimensional regression, yet their conditioning and noise bounds must be redone for a bandwidth-shrinking, dimension-growing random local design. Thus the first changed proof step is KBRW's conditional bias/variance decomposition: every pilot, inverse-Gram condition, and correction term must receive explicit privacy error and budget accounting.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit sample-split algorithm and composition proof releasing all pilots, a spectrally stabilized private local Gram inverse, and a clipped higher-order correction, together with a uniform absolute-risk bound whose optimized bandwidth, basis dimension, ridge, clipping, and privacy-budget split match the exact minimax phase theorem.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates why CATE privatization is not ordinary prediction privatization and decomposes the mechanism into private nuisance and target-learning stages.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Observational CATE requires nuisance learning -> privacy must protect every stage without destroying orthogonality -> low-smoothness optimality requires a fully private higher-order learner

method_exemplars.technique: Use higher-order local-polynomial R-learning with localized projection bases, sample splitting, Gram inversion, and a quadratic U-statistic bias correction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the exact nonprivate estimator whose risk must be preserved and identifies each component needing a private implementation.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt positive-definite private second-moment release via regularization, random augmentation, or inverse-Wishart perturbation, with utility controlled through matrix conditioning.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The local R-learner's stability bottleneck is inversion of a sensitive empirical Gram matrix; this paper directly treats private positive-definite Gram release.

method_exemplars.technique: Use parallel sample splitting, private nuisance fitting, sensitivity calibration through orthogonal scores, and output or Gaussian-process perturbation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest end-to-end central-DP observational CATE mechanism, although the destination replaces its ordinary second stage with the localized higher-order construction.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct honest central approximate-DP pointwise confidence intervals for tau(x0) over a fixed Hölder CATE/nuisance class whose coverage accounts jointly for higher-order nuisance bias and privacy noise and whose expected length follows the corresponding pointwise privacy phase diagram.

source_refs.claim: Identifies quantifying uncertainty added by privatization of a causal model or its predictions as a future-research direction.
source_refs.author: Maresa Schröder, Valentyn Melnychuk, Stefan Feuerriegel

source_refs.claim: Provides pointwise absolute-risk optimality for smooth CATE but not privacy-aware confidence intervals or a private limit law.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: Gives differentially private point and interval estimators with consistency and rate guarantees for an observational covariate-balancing average effect, not nonparametric pointwise CATE.
source_refs.author: Yuki Ohnishi, Jordan Awan

source_refs.claim: Builds doubly robust (epsilon,delta)-DP confidence intervals for the population ATE by privatizing both the estimate and variance, leaving pointwise CATE outside its scope.
source_refs.author: Maresa Schröder, Justin Hartenstein, Stefan Feuerriegel

open_problems.why_unsolved: Central-DP CATE work provides private point estimators but leaves privacy-induced causal uncertainty unresolved; central-DP interval work treats regular population-average effects, while KBRW's pointwise target is nonparametric and can require a quadratic correction in the low-smoothness regime. A valid interval must estimate or bound the localized higher-order bias, include privacy noise from every released component, and remain uniform over the full fixed-smoothness class. Neither an ATE influence-function variance calculation nor an ordinary private-regression interval resolves this combined nonregular causal-functional problem.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A confidence-interval construction proving uniform asymptotic coverage at a stated level and matching upper and lower bounds for expected length in each (alpha,beta,gamma,epsilon_n,delta_n) phase, or an impossibility theorem identifying regimes where honest shrinking intervals cannot exist.

writing_exemplar.why: Its future-work discussion directly motivates uncertainty from privatizing causal predictions and naturally narrows to pointwise CATE.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Private CATE point predictions are available -> privacy injects uncertainty absent from ordinary causal intervals -> honest pointwise uncertainty must reflect both nuisance regularity and the privacy phase

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt higher-order influence-function U-statistics and bias-variance balancing for rate-optimal point and interval estimation under low nuisance regularity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination interval needs a limit or concentration argument for the same kind of higher-order correction that drives low-smoothness CATE estimation.

method_exemplars.technique: Separately privatize a doubly robust causal estimate and its variance, then account for both sampling and Gaussian privacy noise in the interval.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves the central approximate-DP uncertainty-accounting problem for ATE; the transfer replaces the regular scalar target with localized nonparametric CATE and higher-order bias.

method_exemplars.technique: Use a two-stage private covariate-balancing construction with joint point and interval guarantees under observational assignment.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies an observational-causal template for treating nuisance balancing, privacy composition, and interval validity in one theorem.

literature_map:
Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (Annals of Statistics 2024; arXiv:2203.00837) give the privacy-free Hölder pointwise-CATE minimax frontier, localized fuzzy-hypothesis lower bound, and higher-order local-polynomial R-learner.
Kennedy (Electronic Journal of Statistics 2023; arXiv:2004.14497) develops oracle inequalities and local-polynomial doubly robust CATE estimation, clarifying the ordinary first-order benchmark.
Robins, Li, Tchetgen, and van der Vaart (2008; arXiv:0805.3040) supply higher-order influence-function and U-statistic machinery for low-regularity nonlinear functionals.
Niu et al. (CLeaR 2022; arXiv:2202.11043) give a private CATE meta-algorithm with private explainable boosting machines, primarily evaluated empirically.
Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel (ICLR 2025; arXiv:2503.03486) give central approximate-DP Neyman-orthogonal CATE releases and quasi-oracle conditions, but no Hölder minimax phase theorem.
That ICLR paper identifies uncertainty added by privatization of causal models or predictions as unresolved.
Hall, Rinaldo, and Wasserman (JMLR 2013; arXiv:1203.2570) calibrate Gaussian-process noise by RKHS sensitivity for private function release.
Acharya, Sun, and Zhang (ALT 2021; arXiv:2004.06830) formulate central-DP Le Cam, Fano, and Assouad bounds through couplings and expected Hamming distance.
Cai, Wang, and Zhang (arXiv:2303.07152) develop a score/tracing attack and apply it to Sobolev nonparametric regression, but not causal prior mixtures.
Kamath, Mouzakis, and Singhal (NeurIPS 2022; arXiv:2205.08532) sharpen approximate-DP lower bounds via generalized fingerprinting and private Assouad.
Cai, Chakraborty, and Vuursteen (arXiv:2406.06755) prove near-matching pointwise nonparametric-regression rates under heterogeneous distributed DP, furnishing a nearby gamma-regression benchmark but not the single-curator experiment.
Sheffet (ALT 2019; arXiv:1507.00056) gives positive-definite private second-moment releases, but only for finite-dimensional linear regression.
Ohnishi and Awan (arXiv:2410.14789) and Schröder, Hartenstein, and Feuerriegel (arXiv:2505.21641) provide private causal intervals for average effects, leaving low-regularity pointwise CATE inference open.
The central tension is genuine: the literature contains the nonprivate alpha+beta fuzzy-mixture phenomenon and separate private regression/tracing tools, but no result proving that cancellation survives low-cost replacement-DP transport on the unchanged positive common-support CATE class.
